Watkins Glen International — survey report

Circuit id watkins_glen · USA · theme green (autumn hardwood), day-only, night:false · branch cursor/watkins_glen-survey-a1 @ 272008b (survey commit follows) · 66 frames · read-only survey (no js/css edits) · generated 2026-10-15

Summary

Headline: the circuit builds clean (verify-track OK, audit-circuit all six checks green) but the layout is the weak part. The OSM trace that feeds path was decimated so hard that the Esses, the footbridge and the Sahlen hillside all sit on one 828 m near-straight (lap 0.249–0.402); the real Esses corners do not exist in the centreline. The Esses 4.5° camber zone lands on Turn 1 instead. Source claims, measurements and guesses are labelled below.

Ranked defects (not applied — suggestions only)

D1 · Layout (high) — the Esses are not in the centreline. measured
Built curvature has no peak tighter than R=120 m between lap 0.127 and 0.405, and the 828 m straight 0.249–0.402 carries the "Esses" tyre wall/gravel (scenery/watkins_glen.js:284-286), the Sahlen hillside and stand (:290-334), the −12 m drop (watkins_glen.js:42) and the footbridge (:409-445). Cause: the OSM trace in path (js/circuits/watkins_glen.js:72) jumps [-335.3,211.3] → [-361.4,-567.8] — a 780 m chord — so the real left-right Esses collapsed into one straight. Frames 03, 04, 05 (0.33/0.50 orbit) show a dead-straight road through a tunnel of trees. Suggested fix: re-run tools/track/import-circuit-path.mjs with a denser trace (or hand-author Esses control points), then re-seat turns, sectors, banking and every Esses-keyed prop. Hand to new-track.
D2 · Banking lands on the wrong corner (medium). measured
bankZones[0] = { turn: 1, angleDeg: 4.5, widthM: 150 } (watkins_glen.js:53). turn is 1-based into def.turns (js/track/core/mesh.js:71-74), so it resolves to turns[0] = 0.0645 — Turn 1. Measured lift windows are 0.052–0.078 (1.17 m), 0.610–0.631, 0.915–0.937; nothing at 0.24. The comment on that line ("the Esses; re-seated frac 0.24") is stale, and the brief's "4.5° camber through the drop" is not delivered. Turn 10 → turns[9] = 0.9255 is correct (the Anvil). Fix once D1 lands: either add an Esses apex to turns or use { frac: … }.
D3 · Blue Armco not visible in any frame (medium, mechanism unconfirmed). observed; cause not verified
Seven runs are authored at 5.5 m (scenery/watkins_glen.js:366-374) but none of the six eye frames (61–66) nor the orbit frames show any rail at the 13 m offset; the only barrier-like shapes are the pit-lane wall and a dark low slab at 0.50 (frame 64). Guardrails are emitted through ctx.instance (js/track/scenery/structures.js:223-277) and silently skipped when onTrack(p, railMargin) is true (:241-244); recordBarrier still tightens the driving limit regardless (:227). Possible causes: instanced batches not drawn by the survey build, dedupe via alreadyLaid (:225), or the 254 suppressed tree guard drops reported by verify-track. A numeric probe (__apex.scene()) is the next step — not run here.
D4 · Maple crowns read as tilted slabs (medium). observed; mechanism is a guess
Front-rank maples (scenery/watkins_glen.js:42-55) are three frustum lobes offset by rr = h·0.16 at 120° spacing plus a cone. At orbit/eye distance (frames 03, 63, 33) the lobes read as flat plates sheared off the trunk rather than rounded crowns — the brief's "broad lobed low crown" is not achieved. Suggested: larger lobe radii relative to offset, slight vertical overlap, or reuse the shared tree() crown with a colour override.
D5 · Weather response (medium, engine-level, not circuit data). observed
Fog (frames 25-30): the sky stays saturated blue; only ground haze and the far ridges fade. Storm (31-36): ground and road go dark and mirror-wet but conifers/maples are bleached pale (frames 34-35), so props and ground disagree on exposure. Rain at day (13-18) is still dusk-dark even with PR #1979 merged. Wet/rain reflections of tree crowns are strong and read well. Suspect js/lighting/atmosphere.js (changed by the merged lighting branch); not a Watkins Glen data problem.
D6 · Pit garages read as a blank slab from the track side (low–medium). observed; mechanism is a guess
In frames 01, 31, 49 the long garage block is a flat grey wall with no visible roll-up doors. The door boxes (scenery/watkins_glen.js:111-114) are 0.35 m thick centred 5.4 m inboard of a body whose face is at 5.5 m, so they stand only ≈7 cm proud of the face and are easy to lose in depth/lighting. The brief wants "corrugated roll-up doors with guide rails" as the identity. Suggested: push doors to ≥0.25 m proud.
D7 · Night/dusk: no trackside lighting beyond the pit straight (low, by design). source + observed
night:false and furniture.lamp:"none" (watkins_glen.js:16,66); frames 37-60 show lamp heads and pooled light on the pit straight only, everywhere else the car's headlight pool lights the verge with visibly blocky (coarse vertex-lit) shading on sand and trees. The real circuit has no permanent lighting, so this is acceptable; the blockiness is a renderer/terrain-resolution issue. Night sky is pure black (no stars/moon glow).
D8 · Lake band contradicts the brief (low). source vs brief
waterBand(0.11, 0.23, -1, 280, 480, …) (scenery/watkins_glen.js:387) places Seneca Lake 280–480 m left; the brief says the lake is not visible from most of the circuit and only a distant backdrop "may remain". A pale water strip is visible at the horizon in frame 03.
D9 · Audit residue (low). ground-audit reports 1 buried prim (within baseline); verify-track logs suppressed tree=254 — 254 front-rank/forest trees dropped by guards, which thins the woods the brief calls the whole look. Source of the drops is not attributed per site here.

Code & scenery deep-dive

Def (js/circuits/watkins_glen.js, 75 lines)

  • Geometry source (:69-72): 85 OSM points (closed chord length 5454 m = path.len); the built centreline is 5421.3 m. Gaps in the point list are the root of D1: measured chords of 780 m (points 25→26), 538 m (59→60, another straight with no vertices), 336, 332, 311 and 294 m.
  • Frac tables: elevations (:40-46) are in racing-lap fracs and reproduce exactly in the build (−11.9 / +13.1 m measured). hwZones (:47-51) use control-index fracs (the comments note the arc equivalents). bankZones mix turn, frac, turn — see D2. No _sceneryShift is set (rotation compensation inactive).
  • Turn table (:65): 11 curvature peaks; two pairs (T2/T3 0.5055/0.5255, T10/T11 0.9255/0.932) are close enough to read as one corner each. The Outer Loop (0.405–0.447, R≈59–117 m over ~230 m) has no turn entry.
  • Exclusions (:22-25): foliage suppressed 0.93–0.08 and 0.24–0.34 — the scenery file duplicates this with its own openArea() gate (scenery:66), so the shared pass and the custom maple pass agree only by convention.
  • Kit: rail:"armco", tyre:"stack", standSet:["scaffold","alu","concrete"], tree broadleafFall with fol [0.56,0.30,0.13].

Scenery (js/circuits/scenery/watkins_glen.js, 656 lines)

  • Lap-fraction anchors all use the wrapped helpers (K(), anchor(), guardrail() …), so they are authored-frame fracs — consistent with the engine's compensation rule; none pre-shifts.
  • Hero model groups required by the landmark file: glen-pit-garages (:103), glen-timing-tower (:133), glen-pit-terrace (:176), glen-esses-hill (:302) plus watkins-footbridge piers. The registry JSON lists only three of them (not the garages or footbridge) — fine, the test only demands each listed id exist.
  • Budget discipline is visible in comments ("blew the props-tris ratchet", baseline 336 038 tris; current compaction 339 556). The Pit Terrace, Esses stand and tower deliberately skip per-seat geometry; the four bleachers use per-seat coat boxes at 0.8 m pitch (:256-261) — the largest tri consumer in the file.
  • Terrain-seat patterns: liftToTerrain (:17-26), per-tent terrainYAt clamps (:462-463, :527-529) and the RV camp's lowest-corner seating (:567-581) are why the float/ground audits are clean; the comments record the earlier floating fire pit and bog-bury regressions.
  • No lamp, floodlight or night emitter exists in the file; only three camera masts (:617-621) and two gantries (:206-207) — consistent with D7.
  • Ridge backdrop (:390-407): three rings of 50/40/30 hash-placed ridge slabs; they appear as dark flat trapezoids on the horizon in every orbit frame (frames 01, 03, 05) — they read as low-poly walls rather than hills.

Real-world cross-check

The brief cites Wikipedia (Watkins Glen International: 2006 tower rebuild, Nazareth stands 2005, Boot added 1971), theglen.com facility maps and theglenrace.com grandstand map. This survey did not re-fetch those URLs; all real-world statements above are the brief's, not independently verified. Length: the real GP-era layout is ≈5.43 km, built 5.42 km (−0.2 %) — consistent. Turn count (11) matches the brief; the geometry that is wrong is the Esses (D1), not the count.

Not captured / uncertain

  • Cut from the plan: trackside camera frames (orbit and six eye frames only; eye only at day/dry), dawn, and eye/trackside views for wet, rain, fog, storm and night. Frames are at six lap fractions (0, 0.17, 0.33, 0.50, 0.67, 0.83) — no frame at the footbridge (0.365), the Outer Loop (0.42) or the Anvil (0.90) proper.
  • Orbit frames show one car; fog frame 27 shows a field on track — race state differs between groups, so car presence is not a defect signal.
  • D3 (Armco), D4 and D6 mechanisms are hypotheses; no numeric probe (__apex) or per-site prop attribution was run. graph-parity was not run.
  • Renderer: TLX under SwiftShader (no GPU); soft-shadow/bloom differences on a real GPU are not represented.
  • Weather arc (js/race/weather-arc.js) transitions were not exercised — only static --weather states.
